commitResults.messageBody: Save the task list whenever a command changes it. Store task details in a relative text file with encoded fields so user input cannot corrupt record separators.
Restore task types and completion statuses when Quackie starts. Return an empty list when the data file does not exist so a first run needs no setup.
Keep Quackie usable when saved data is malformed or storage writes fail. Report the problem to the user and continue with an empty task list when loading cannot be completed.
Verify that a completed deadline retains its status after a restart. Remove the empty data directory in the fixture so the test also covers creating the relative storage folder.
Number the test-plan headings in execution order so the test-ui console record is easier to follow without changing any expected behaviour.
Parse recognised deadline values into Java date types so Quackie can validate and display dates consistently. Retain free-form values for backward compatibility.
Separate parsing, storage, user interaction, and task-list state from the main application loop. This gives each responsibility a focused home while preserving existing behaviour.
Represent parsed user actions as command objects so parsing and execution can evolve independently. This completes the optional command-hierarchy extension.
Group commands, parsing, storage, tasks, and user interaction into cohesive packages. This makes ownership clearer as the codebase grows.
Add a Gradle wrapper and application configuration so contributors can compile and run Quackie with a consistent build tool.
Exercise command parsing, task behaviour, persistence, and user interaction with focused unit tests. Small dependency-injection seams keep the tests isolated and deterministic.
Require the Gradle unit-test suite after code changes so future increments preserve both internal behaviour and the command-line contract.
Configure the Shadow plugin to produce a self-contained quackie.jar with the application entry point in its manifest. Generated binaries remain outside version control.
Document application entry points, command contracts, parser construction, and task state so the generated API reference explains the non-obvious public surface.

Use explicit imports, immutable event fields, and consistent dependency ordering throughout the affected source and test files. These mechanical changes improve readability without changing behaviour.
Record the uploaded Java, Markdown, and Git conventions in the repository guidance so later changes follow the same rules consistently.

Implement find as a command that matches keywords within task descriptions while preserving task order. Validate missing keywords and cover matches, case differences, and empty results in UI and unit tests.
Add the SE-EDU-aligned Checkstyle rules to the Gradle lifecycle and fix existing source and test formatting violations so clean builds enforce the project standard.

Connect a polished chat interface to the existing command and storage
logic so users can manage tasks without the console. Add JavaFX
integration tests and preserve the command-line regression suite.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use varargs for grouped UI messages
commitResults.messageBody:
Introduce a focused helper for printing any number of related message
lines. This removes repeated output calls while preserving the existing
console and GUI responses.

Assert non-null contracts at parser, task-list, and storage boundaries.
These values are guaranteed by Quackie's control flow, so assertion failures
identify programming defects without replacing user-facing validation.

Extract the duplicated numbered-list loop used by list and find output.
Keeping the formatting in one helper makes future presentation changes safer
and prevents the two views from drifting apart.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use a stream to filter matching tasks
commitResults.messageBody:
Replace the manual search loop with a stream over the populated array
range. The filter states the search condition directly while retaining task
order and excluding unused null slots.

Consolidate task list rendering

commitResults.messageTitle: Allow tasks to be updated in place
commitResults.messageBody: Add an update command that replaces a task's details while retaining its list position and completion status. Validate the task number and replacement command before mutation, then persist successful updates immediately. Document the syntax and cover parsing, execution, persistence, and invalid input in JUnit and UI tests.
Allow tasks to be updated in place
Give invalid commands a distinct visual treatment so errors are easier to notice. Add a compact status badge and refine the conversation background without changing command-line behaviour.
Use a duck avatar, playful welcome, and pond-themed interface copy to make the chatbot memorable while keeping task responses concise.

Normalise harmless whitespace, reject ambiguous markers and duplicate tasks, validate structured event ranges, and report full task lists clearly. Extend JUnit and scripted UI coverage for the new failure modes.
Cover corrupted storage, write failures, full-list handling, free-form dates, command recognition, GUI error styling, special characters, and additional model boundary cases.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix task count grammar and event time display
commitResults.messageBody:
The add and delete confirmations always said "N tasks", producing
"1 tasks" for a single task. Both now use a shared formatTaskCount
helper that picks the singular noun only for exactly one task.

Structured event times were validated but then printed exactly as
typed, while deadlines showed the same format in a friendly form.
Events now keep the parsed times and display them with the same
formatter as deadlines, now shared in Task. The raw values are still
stored, so the save file format and duplicate detection are unchanged.
